column3: Back
column4: Explanation
column5: Tags

column2: What is the core difference between Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS?
column3: SQS stores messages in a queue for consumers to poll and process; SNS pushes each publication to subscribed endpoints.
column4: SQS supports decoupled work queues, while SNS supports publish/subscribe fan-out.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Messaging topic::Decoupling

column2: An order-processing service must absorb traffic spikes and let workers process jobs independently. Which service is the best fit?
column3: Amazon SQS.
column4: A queue buffers work and decouples producers from consumers so each side can scale independently.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Messaging topic::Asynchronous_processing

column2: One alarm must notify email recipients, a Lambda function, and an SQS queue at the same time. Which service fits?
column3: Amazon SNS.
column4: An SNS topic can fan one publication out to multiple subscribed endpoints.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Messaging topic::Fan-out

column2: What does Amazon EC2 provide?
column3: Resizable virtual compute instances in AWS.
column4: EC2 gives customers control of the guest operating system and application stack on virtual machines.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Compute topic::Virtual_machines

column2: A team needs MySQL but wants AWS to manage the underlying database infrastructure and routine platform operations. Which service should it evaluate?
column3: Amazon RDS.
column4: RDS is a managed relational database service; the customer still owns data, access, schemas, and configuration choices.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Databases topic::Managed_services

column2: What does Infrastructure as a Service provide, and what major control remains with the customer?
column3: It provides virtualized infrastructure; the customer retains control of the guest operating system, applications, data, and many configurations.
column4: IaaS removes physical-hardware ownership without removing workload administration.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Service_models topic::IaaS

column2: How are the AWS Management Console, CLI, SDKs, and IaC tools related to AWS service APIs?
column3: They are different interfaces that ultimately invoke AWS service APIs.
column4: “Single unified API” is only a mental model; it is not the name of one AWS product or one literal endpoint.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::APIs topic::Cloud_management

column2: What benefits does Infrastructure as Code provide?
column3: Repeatable, version-controlled, reviewable, and automated infrastructure provisioning.
column4: Machine-readable definitions reduce manual configuration drift and support consistent environments.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Automation

column2: Why is Terraform better described as an orchestrator than as an application compiler?
column3: It builds a plan and calls provider APIs to reach a desired infrastructure state; it does not produce an application binary.
column4: Terraform reads HCL and coordinates resource changes through provider APIs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Terraform

column2: Complete the relationship: An AWS Region contains multiple isolated ________.
column3: Availability Zones.
column4: Regions are separate geographic areas, and multi-AZ design provides isolation within a Region.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::cloze topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Regions

column2: What is an Availability Zone?
column3: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region.
column4: AZs are designed for fault isolation while maintaining low-latency connectivity to other AZs in the Region.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Availability_Zones

column2: What is the geographic scope of an Amazon VPC?
column3: A VPC belongs to one AWS Region and can span that Region’s Availability Zones.
column4: Subnets divide the VPC at the AZ level.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Networking topic::VPC_scope

column2: Can one subnet span multiple Availability Zones?
column3: No. A subnet resides entirely within one Availability Zone.
column4: An Availability Zone can contain multiple subnets, but a subnet cannot cross AZ boundaries.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Subnets

column2: An EC2 instance is placed in a subnet whose route table has a route to an internet gateway. Is the instance automatically reachable from the internet?
column3: No. It also needs an appropriate public address and security rules that allow the traffic.
column4: A route makes the subnet public, but internet reachability depends on routing, addressing, and filtering together.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Networking topic::Public_subnets

column2: Why might `us-east-1a` refer to different physical zones in two AWS accounts?
column3: Availability Zone letter mappings can differ by account.
column4: Use AZ IDs when different accounts must coordinate on the same physical Availability Zone.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Availability_Zone_IDs

column2: How can an S3 bucket be Regional while its name is globally unique?
column3: The bucket’s data resides in a selected Region, while its name must be unique across the general-purpose bucket namespace.
column4: A global console view and global naming do not mean that bucket data is automatically stored worldwide.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Storage topic::Global_infrastructure

column2: Which THREE factors commonly influence AWS Region selection?
column3: Latency to users, regulatory or data-location requirements, and service availability or price.
column4: Region choice is a business and technical decision; no single Region is best for every workload.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::multiple-response topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Region_selection

column2: Which two practices best protect the AWS account root user?
column3: Enable MFA and reserve the root user for tasks that explicitly require it.
column4: The root user has unrestricted account access and should not be used for routine administration.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Root_user topic::MFA

column2: Does an IAM user require its own external email address or payment method?
column3: No. It is an identity defined inside one AWS account.
column4: Usage performed by the IAM user is billed to the AWS account.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::IAM_users topic::Identities

column2: Distinguish authentication from authorization.
column3: Authentication verifies who the caller is; authorization determines what that identity may do.
column4: Both are required to securely evaluate AWS requests.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Authentication topic::Authorization

column2: What permissions does a newly created IAM identity receive merely by existing?
column3: None. Permissions must be granted through applicable authorization policies and mechanisms.
column4: AWS access is not granted automatically to a new identity.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::IAM_policies topic::Default_permissions

column2: Complete the common IAM policy elements: Effect, Action, Resource, and optional ________.
column3: Condition.
column4: Conditions narrow when a statement applies, such as by source, time, tags, or other context keys.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::cloze topic::IAM_policies topic::JSON

column2: A developer needs read access to one S3 bucket for one project. Which approach follows least privilege?
column3: Grant only the required read actions on that bucket, not broad administrator or all-S3 permissions.
column4: Least privilege limits permissions to the task and resource actually required.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Least_privilege topic::IAM_policies

column2: What are the two parts of an IAM access key?
column3: An access key ID and a secret access key.
column4: Both are used to sign programmatic requests; the secret access key is retrievable only when created.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Access_keys topic::Programmatic_access

column2: How can an IAM user rotate an access key without an abrupt application outage?
column3: Create the second key, update and test the application, then deactivate and delete the old key.
column4: An IAM user can have at most two access keys, which supports an overlap during rotation.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Access_keys topic::Rotation

column2: What is the preferred alternative to long-lived access keys for AWS workloads?
column3: IAM roles and temporary security credentials.
column4: Temporary credentials reduce the risk and maintenance burden of static secrets.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Temporary_credentials topic::IAM_roles

column2: Who patches the guest operating system on an Amazon EC2 instance?
column3: The customer.
column4: AWS secures the physical infrastructure and virtualization layer; the customer manages the guest OS and applications.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Shared_responsibility topic::EC2

column2: Which Lambda security responsibilities remain with the customer?
column3: Function code and libraries, data, IAM permissions, and resource configuration.
column4: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, operating system, and managed runtime platform.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Shared_responsibility topic::Serverless

column2: Do service control policies grant permissions?
column3: No. SCPs set the maximum available permissions for principals in member accounts.
column4: IAM or resource policies must still grant access, and an explicit restriction from an applicable SCP limits the result.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Organizations topic::Service_control_policies

column2: A company needs to record resource configurations and evaluate them continuously against rules. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Config.
column4: AWS Config records supported configuration history and evaluates compliance. Remediation is optional and must be configured.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Compliance topic::Configuration_auditing

column2: Distinguish data residency from data sovereignty.
column3: Residency is where data is physically stored; sovereignty is the legal jurisdiction and authority governing it.
column4: Compliance requirements may impose controls based on both location and jurisdiction.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Compliance topic::Data_governance

column2: Which AWS environment is designed for eligible U.S. government and highly regulated workloads with isolated Regions?
column3: AWS GovCloud (US).
column4: GovCloud has specific eligibility and access requirements; it is not simply a general Region available to any individual.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Compliance topic::Government_workloads

column2: List the defining characteristics of a security group.
column3: It is stateful, applies at the resource network-interface level, and supports allow rules only.
column4: Security groups evaluate all applicable rules and automatically allow response traffic for an allowed flow.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Security_groups

column2: List the defining characteristics of a network ACL.
column3: It is stateless, applies at subnet boundaries, supports allow and deny rules, and processes numbered rules in ascending order.
column4: Inbound and outbound traffic are evaluated separately.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Network_ACLs

column2: When should a security group be preferred over a network ACL?
column3: Use security groups for fine-grained resource access; use NACLs as coarse-grained subnet guardrails or defense in depth.
column4: Security groups are more versatile because they are stateful and can reference other security groups.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Network_security

column2: A security group allows an inbound HTTPS request. Must a separate outbound rule allow the response to that request?
column3: No. Response traffic is automatically allowed because security groups are stateful.
column4: State tracking permits the return flow regardless of outbound rules.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Stateful_firewalls

column2: Which VPC control can explicitly deny a known malicious IP range for an entire subnet?
column3: A network ACL.
column4: NACLs support deny rules at subnet boundaries; security groups support allow rules only.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Explicit_deny

column2: Is an S3 bucket placed inside a customer VPC subnet?
column3: No. S3 is a managed Regional service outside customer subnets.
column4: VPC resources can reach S3 through public service endpoints or supported VPC endpoints.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Storage topic::VPC_architecture

column2: Which services support gateway VPC endpoints, and what is the endpoint charge?
column3: Amazon S3 and DynamoDB; there is no additional charge for the gateway endpoint.
column4: Gateway endpoints add service-prefix routes to selected VPC route tables.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::VPC_endpoints topic::Gateway_endpoints

column2: How does an interface VPC endpoint connect a VPC privately to a service?
column3: It creates elastic network interfaces with private IP addresses and uses AWS PrivateLink.
column4: Interface endpoints can use security groups and normally incur endpoint-hour and data-processing charges.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::VPC_endpoints topic::Interface_endpoints

column2: EC2 instances in a private subnet need ordinary same-Region access to S3 without a NAT gateway and without an endpoint-hour charge. What should be used?
column3: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint.
column4: A gateway endpoint routes S3 traffic through selected route tables with no additional endpoint charge.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::VPC_endpoints topic::Service_selection

column2: A company needs a dedicated, predictable network connection from its data center to AWS. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Direct Connect.
column4: Direct Connect establishes dedicated connectivity for hybrid bandwidth and consistency requirements.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Hybrid_networking

column2: Which service caches HTTP/HTTPS content at edge locations close to viewers?
column3: Amazon CloudFront.
column4: CloudFront is AWS’s content delivery network and reduces origin load and viewer latency.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Content_delivery topic::Caching

column2: What does a CloudFront invalidation do?
column3: It removes selected objects from CloudFront caches before their normal expiration.
column4: Use invalidation when updated content must be fetched from the origin before its TTL expires.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Content_delivery topic::Caching

column2: What does AWS Global Accelerator provide for an IPv4 accelerator by default?
column3: Two static anycast IPv4 addresses that route supported traffic through the AWS global network.
column4: Global Accelerator improves network-path performance and failover without caching application content.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Network_acceleration topic::Anycast

column2: When should CloudFront be selected instead of Global Accelerator?
column3: Choose CloudFront when HTTP/HTTPS content should be cached; choose Global Accelerator for network acceleration and static anycast entry points without caching.
column4: Both use edge infrastructure, but they solve different layers of the problem.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Content_delivery topic::Network_acceleration

column2: Globally distributed users must upload large files to one distant S3 bucket faster. Which feature should be evaluated?
column3: S3 Transfer Acceleration.
column4: It uses AWS edge infrastructure and optimized network paths for long-distance S3 transfers.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Data_transfer topic::Edge_networking

column2: Distinguish AWS Local Zones from AWS Wavelength.
column3: Local Zones place selected AWS infrastructure near metro areas; Wavelength places infrastructure within communications-provider networks for carrier-edge workloads.
column4: Both reduce latency, but the target access environment differs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Edge_computing

column2: A workload needs AWS-managed infrastructure installed at the customer’s premises for local processing. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Outposts.
column4: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure, APIs, and selected services to customer locations.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Hybrid_cloud topic::On-premises

column2: What storage model does Amazon S3 provide?
column3: Regional object storage accessed through APIs.
column4: S3 stores objects in buckets; prefixes create a folder-like view but not a traditional mounted file system.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Storage topic::Object_storage

column2: What storage model does Amazon EBS provide?
column3: Durable block storage volumes for Amazon EC2.
column4: An EBS volume behaves like a block device and must be in the same AZ as the attached instance.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Storage topic::Block_storage

column2: Is it always true that one EBS volume can attach to only one EC2 instance?
column3: No. That is the normal model, but supported io1/io2 volumes can use Multi-Attach with multiple Nitro-based instances in the same AZ.
column4: Multi-Attach is constrained and requires applications or clustered file systems that safely coordinate writes.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Storage topic::Multi-Attach

column2: What storage model and protocol does Amazon EFS provide?
column3: Elastic shared file storage using NFS.
column4: Multiple compute instances can mount the same EFS file system. EFS does not provide SMB.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Storage topic::File_storage

column2: Match S3, EBS, and EFS to their primary access models.
column3: S3 = object/API; EBS = EC2 block device; EFS = shared NFS file system.
column4: Choose storage by access semantics, sharing, and workload needs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Storage topic::Service_selection

column2: Does an EBS volume always survive termination of its EC2 instance?
column3: Not always. EBS can persist independently, but a delete-on-termination setting may remove it.
column4: Persistence capability and lifecycle configuration are different facts.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Storage topic::Persistence

column2: What persistent storage does a standard AWS CloudShell environment provide?
column3: A 1 GB home directory per supported Region, retained until 120 days of inactivity in that Region.
column4: Temporary storage outside the home directory is recycled; CloudShell VPC environments do not have the same persistent home storage.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Developer_tools topic::Persistent_storage

column2: What are the main functions of Amazon CloudWatch?
column3: Collect metrics and logs, visualize dashboards, and create alarms and automated responses.
column4: CloudWatch focuses on operational telemetry and application/resource health.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Monitoring topic::Observability

column2: An administrator wants EC2 guest-memory utilization in CloudWatch. Is it available as a standard EC2 metric?
column3: No. Install the CloudWatch agent or publish a custom metric.
column4: The EC2 service exposes infrastructure metrics such as CPU, but guest OS memory requires in-instance telemetry.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Monitoring topic::EC2_metrics

column2: Does creating an AWS Budget automatically impose a hard spending cap?
column3: No. Budgets monitor thresholds and notify; optional budget actions must be configured separately.
column4: Resources keep running by default after a budget threshold is crossed.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Cost_management topic::Budgets

column2: When should AWS Budgets be used instead of AWS Cost Explorer?
column3: Use Budgets for thresholds, alerts, and optional actions; use Cost Explorer to analyze and visualize cost and usage trends.
column4: One watches against a target; the other supports investigation and analysis.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Cost_management

column2: Distinguish CloudWatch from AWS Budgets.
column3: CloudWatch monitors operational telemetry; AWS Budgets tracks cost or usage against financial or consumption thresholds.
column4: Both can alert, but they observe different data and answer different questions.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Monitoring topic::Cost_management

column2: A short-term, irregular EC2 workload cannot be interrupted and has no predictable long-term baseline. Which pricing model fits?
column3: On-Demand Instances.
column4: On-Demand requires no long-term commitment and suits irregular non-interruptible use.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::EC2_pricing topic::On-Demand

column2: A fault-tolerant batch workload can handle interruption and should minimize EC2 cost. Which capacity fits?
column3: EC2 Spot Instances.
column4: Spot uses spare capacity at a large discount but can be interrupted.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::EC2_pricing topic::Spot

column2: What commitment is exchanged for Savings Plans discounts?
column3: A consistent amount of eligible compute usage, measured in dollars per hour, for one or three years.
column4: Savings Plans are more flexible than EC2 Reserved Instances across eligible compute usage.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Pricing_models topic::Savings_Plans

column2: Are EC2 Reserved Instances separate physical servers?
column3: No. They are a billing discount applied to matching On-Demand usage; some zonal RIs also provide a capacity-reservation benefit.
column4: The term describes a pricing benefit, not a special instance object running by itself.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Pricing_models topic::Reserved_Instances

column2: How does a container differ from a virtual machine?
column3: A container shares a host OS kernel, while a virtual machine includes a guest OS on virtualized hardware.
column4: Containers are typically lighter and start faster; VMs provide a separate guest OS boundary.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Compute_models topic::Containers

column2: Is a cluster itself an orchestrator?
column3: No. A cluster is a logical grouping or capacity boundary; ECS or EKS provides orchestration.
column4: Scaling capacity and distributing traffic are handled by services such as Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing, not by the word “cluster” itself.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Containers topic::Clusters

column2: Distinguish ECS, EKS, and Fargate.
column3: ECS is AWS container orchestration, EKS is managed Kubernetes, and Fargate provides serverless compute capacity for supported ECS or EKS workloads.
column4: Fargate is a compute option, not a third competing orchestrator.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Containers topic::Serverless

column2: Which AWS service stores private container images for later deployment?
column3: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR).
column4: ECR is a managed container image registry integrated with AWS container services.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Containers topic::Registries

column2: Developers want to upload web application code while AWS provisions load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
column4: Beanstalk orchestrates underlying AWS resources while the team retains visibility and control of them.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Application_deployment topic::Managed_platforms

column2: A small business wants a simple bundled VPS with predictable monthly pricing for a basic website. Which service fits?
column3: Amazon Lightsail.
column4: Lightsail packages simplified compute, storage, networking, and plans for straightforward workloads.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Compute topic::Simple_hosting

column2: When should Lightsail be chosen instead of Elastic Beanstalk?
column3: Choose Lightsail for a simple bundled VPS and predictable plan; choose Beanstalk for code-centric deployment on scalable standard AWS resources.
column4: Both simplify deployment, but their abstraction and scaling models differ.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Application_deployment

column2: Which service schedules batch jobs and provisions supported compute environments to run them?
column3: AWS Batch.
column4: AWS Batch is designed for queued batch workloads and can use Spot capacity when interruptions are acceptable.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Batch_computing

column2: A company wants utilization-based rightsizing recommendations without automatically changing resources. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Compute Optimizer.
column4: Compute Optimizer analyzes metrics and configurations to produce recommendations; the customer decides whether to apply them.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Cost_optimization topic::Rightsizing

column2: What is the AWS Nitro System’s role in modern EC2?
column3: It uses dedicated hardware and a lightweight hypervisor architecture to offload and isolate many networking, storage, management, and security functions.
column4: Nitro reduces virtualization overhead and enables capabilities such as EC2 bare metal integration.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Compute_architecture topic::Virtualization

column2: A workload requires direct access to physical server hardware while retaining VPC and EBS integration. Which EC2 option fits?
column3: An EC2 bare metal instance type.
column4: Nitro-based bare metal provides direct hardware access within the EC2 service model.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Compute topic::Bare_metal

column2: What is Bottlerocket?
column3: An AWS-sponsored minimal Linux-based operating system designed for hosting containers.
column4: Its reduced package surface and transactional update model target secure container hosts.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Containers topic::Operating_systems

column2: What does AWS ParallelCluster automate?
column3: Creation and management of HPC clusters on AWS from configuration and command-line workflows.
column4: It provisions components such as head and compute nodes and integrates with HPC schedulers.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::High-performance_computing topic::Cluster_management

column2: Tightly coupled HPC nodes need very low inter-instance latency. Which combination should be evaluated?
column3: A cluster placement group with Elastic Fabric Adapter on supported EC2 instances.
column4: Cluster placement provides close placement in one AZ; EFA supports high-performance inter-instance communication.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::High-performance_computing topic::Networking

column2: Which service provides a high-performance parallel file system commonly used by HPC workloads?
column3: Amazon FSx for Lustre.
column4: FSx for Lustre is optimized for fast parallel access to large datasets.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::High-performance_computing topic::Storage

column2: What does AWS Ground Station provide?
column3: Managed satellite ground-station capabilities integrated with AWS services.
column4: It lets customers schedule satellite contacts and move received data into AWS for processing and storage.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Satellite_workloads

column2: Distinguish high availability from fault tolerance without using fixed percentages.
column3: High availability minimizes downtime through redundancy and recovery; fault tolerance aims to continue operating despite component failure.
column4: Neither term guarantees one universal SLA or literal 100% availability.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Resilience topic::Availability

column2: Distinguish RTO from RPO.
column3: RTO is maximum acceptable time to restore service; RPO is maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.
column4: RTO looks forward from disruption to recovery; RPO looks backward to the last recoverable point.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Recovery_objectives

column2: Which studied DR strategy generally has the lowest ongoing cost but the longest recovery time?
column3: Backup and restore.
column4: Infrastructure and data are restored after the event, trading low standby cost for higher RTO and often higher RPO.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Backup_and_restore

column2: What remains ready in a pilot-light disaster recovery strategy?
column3: The critical core of the workload, including replicated data, while additional application infrastructure is started or deployed during recovery.
column4: Pilot light costs less than maintaining a fully functional scaled-down environment.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Pilot_light

column2: What distinguishes warm standby from pilot light?
column3: Warm standby keeps a scaled-down but functional copy of the workload running in the recovery location.
column4: It costs more during normal operation but normally recovers faster.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Warm_standby

column2: A company requires faster recovery than pilot light and accepts the cost of a small functional environment running continuously. Which strategy fits?
column3: Warm standby.
column4: The recovery environment already serves as a functional scaled-down copy and can scale after failover.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Strategy_selection

column2: Does multi-site active/active automatically guarantee RPO 0?
column3: No. It can reduce recovery time to near zero, but RPO depends on the data architecture and replication behavior.
column4: Data corruption may still require backups, and active traffic in multiple Regions does not prove synchronous writes.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Active/active

column2: How do synchronous and asynchronous replication affect RPO?
column3: Synchronous replication can target RPO 0 but adds latency and constraints; asynchronous replication can leave a replication lag.
column4: The replication method affects data-loss exposure independently of how quickly compute recovers.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Replication

column2: What does AWS CloudFormation do?
column3: It provisions and manages AWS resources from declarative JSON or YAML templates.
column4: Deployed resources are managed in stacks as logical units.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code

column2: What is a CloudFormation stack?
column3: A collection of AWS resources managed as a single unit from a template.
column4: Creating, updating, and deleting the stack manages the related resources and their dependencies.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Stacks

column2: Does deleting a CloudFormation stack always delete every resource it ever managed?
column3: No. Deletion policies, retained resources, dependencies, or deletion failures can leave resources behind.
column4: CloudFormation deletes managed resources by default, but lifecycle controls and failures are important exceptions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::scenario topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Resource_lifecycle

column2: What happens when `cdk synth` runs?
column3: AWS CDK synthesizes the application’s constructs into a CloudFormation template.
column4: CloudFormation remains the deployment engine for the synthesized infrastructure definition.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::CDK

column2: Distinguish an AWS SDK from AWS CDK.
column3: An SDK invokes AWS APIs from application or automation code; CDK defines infrastructure and synthesizes CloudFormation templates.
column4: Use an SDK for runtime service operations and CDK for infrastructure definitions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::Developer_tools topic::Infrastructure_as_Code

column2: What is an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) used for?
column3: To identify an AWS resource in APIs, policies, and service integrations using a service-specific format.
column4: ARN segments and resource portions vary, and global-resource ARNs can omit the Region segment.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Resource_identifiers

column2: What does AWS Signature Version 4 provide for API requests?
column3: It authenticates the credentialed caller and protects request integrity by signing request data.
column4: SDKs and the CLI normally create the signature automatically from credentials.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::API_security topic::Request_signing

column2: What is the difference between a Regional service endpoint and a global endpoint?
column3: A Regional endpoint targets service API behavior in a named Region; a global endpoint has no Region in the hostname and serves global or centralized behavior.
column4: Endpoint scope and resource scope are related but not always identical, so avoid assuming every URL follows one rule.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::comparison topic::APIs topic::Service_endpoints

column2: Why is calling AWS CDK purely “imperative IaC” incomplete?
column3: CDK code can use imperative language features, but it synthesizes a declarative CloudFormation template that CloudFormation deploys.
column4: The source language and the deployment model are different layers.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::CDK

column2: A company needs to decouple order processing and independently notify several subscribers. Which TWO services meet these separate needs?
column3: Use Amazon SQS for the work queue and Amazon SNS for fan-out notifications.
column4: SQS buffers work for consumers; SNS publishes to multiple subscriptions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::multiple-response topic::Messaging topic::Service_selection

column2: Which TWO actions are recommended for the AWS account root user?
column3: Enable MFA and use root only for tasks that require it.
column4: The root user is unrestricted and should not be used for routine work or programmatic access keys.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::multiple-response topic::Root_user topic::Security_best_practices

column2: A security team must explicitly deny one malicious IP range for every resource in a subnet. Which control should it configure?
column3: A network ACL.
column4: NACLs operate at subnet boundaries and support explicit deny rules; security groups are allow-only.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Network_security

column2: Which statement about VPC network scope is correct?
column3: A VPC spans Availability Zones in one Region, while each subnet belongs to one AZ.
column4: A VPC is Regional and subnets are AZ-scoped.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Networking topic::Global_infrastructure

column2: Which statement correctly describes a general-purpose S3 bucket?
column3: Its data is stored in a selected Region, while its bucket name is globally unique.
column4: Global naming and the global console view do not make the bucket’s data automatically global.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Storage topic::Global_infrastructure

column2: Private EC2 instances need same-Region S3 access without a NAT gateway or additional endpoint charge. Which option is best?
column3: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint.
column4: Gateway endpoints route S3 traffic through selected route tables with no additional endpoint charge.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::VPC_endpoints

column2: A gaming application needs static anycast IP addresses and accelerated UDP traffic without content caching. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Global Accelerator.
column4: Global Accelerator improves network paths for supported TCP/UDP traffic and does not act as a CDN cache.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Content_delivery topic::Network_acceleration

column2: Hundreds of Linux EC2 instances need concurrent access to the same shared directory hierarchy. Which storage service fits?
column3: Amazon EFS.
column4: EFS provides shared NFS file storage that multiple compute instances can mount.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Storage topic::Service_selection

column2: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2. Which TWO tasks are customer responsibilities?
column3: Patching the guest operating system and configuring security groups.
column4: AWS manages the facilities, physical hardware, and virtualization layer.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::multiple-response topic::Shared_responsibility

column2: A rendering workload can checkpoint progress and tolerate interruption. Which EC2 purchase option can provide the largest discount with no long-term commitment?
column3: EC2 Spot Instances.
column4: Spot uses spare capacity at discounted prices and is appropriate for interrupt-tolerant work.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::EC2_pricing topic::Spot

column2: A finance team wants an email when forecast monthly cost exceeds a threshold. Which service should it use?
column3: AWS Budgets.
column4: Budgets evaluates actual or forecast cost/usage against configured thresholds.
column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Cost_management

column2: Which statement about AWS Fargate is correct?
column3: It provides serverless compute capacity for supported ECS and EKS workloads.
column4: ECS and EKS orchestrate containers; Fargate supplies managed compute capacity.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Containers topic::Serverless

column2: A business can tolerate losing at most 15 minutes of transactions after a disaster. Which objective is being specified?
column3: Recovery Point Objective (RPO).
column4: RPO expresses acceptable data loss measured in time before the disruption.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Recovery_objectives

column2: A recovery Region runs a small but fully functional copy of the workload and scales up after failover. Which strategy is this?
column3: Warm standby.
column4: Warm standby keeps reduced-capacity functionality running continuously.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Warm_standby

column2: Which statement about multi-site active/active is most accurate?
column3: It can reduce RTO to near zero, but RPO still depends on the data architecture and replication behavior.
column4: Serving traffic from several Regions does not automatically guarantee synchronous writes or zero data loss.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Disaster_recovery topic::Active/active

column2: What is the direct output of `cdk synth`?
column3: A CloudFormation template.
column4: CDK constructs written in supported programming languages synthesize into the declarative template deployed by CloudFormation.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::CDK

column2: An application runs on EC2 and needs access to S3. What is the preferred credential approach?
column3: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance and use temporary credentials.
column4: Roles avoid embedding long-lived access keys in application files.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Access_keys topic::Temporary_credentials

column2: A factory must run AWS-managed infrastructure inside its own facility for local processing. Which service is designed for this?
column3: AWS Outposts.
column4: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and selected services to customer premises.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 type::single-choice topic::Edge_computing topic::Hybrid_cloud
